name: Strange Bones: Curiosities of the Human Skeleton
description: This exhibition will focus on the many different strange, odd, and curious things that happen to our skeletons.  In addition to information on bone remodeling and adaptation, examples of skeletal congenital anomalies, diseases that disfigure the skeleton, strange healing patterns of traumatic injuries, and cultural modification of the skeleton and teeth will be highlighted.  This exhibition will scientifically focus on how the human skeleton is extremely interesting and adaptable, and will teach our visitors about the biological forces behind certain skeletal diseases and disfiguration.

name: miXtape
description: Take a seriously wild musical ride back to the most awesome of decades.  Reagan was in the White House, Michael Jackson was at the top of the charts, lycra and legwarmers were the accessories du jour, and a “mix tape” of favorite tunes was the ultimate in self-expression.  The lousy economy was about to bounce back like we’d never seen, set to the synthesized beat of 80s Rock.  The Cold War was heating up, and with fingers on the nuclear button, the world was sure to end any moment.  But for Generation X, life was just beginning.  Put on your suspenders, pull out the Members Only jacket, do your hair up with a scrunchy, and “everybody cut footloose” with us in this totally rad musical world premiere.

name: Fireworks and BBQ - 4th of July on the Berkeley ferry
description: 4th of July Fireworks and BBQ in San Diego! Celebrate with family, friends and the supporters of the Maritime Museum of San Diego with a BBQ dinner, live entertainment, photo opportunites, and views of incredible fireworks from multiple locations. The evening begins on the beautiful 1898 steam ferry Berkeley where we'll enjoy a delicious BBQ dinner and entertainment on the strategically located Berkeley upper deck. After dinner, you can relocate and find your preferred spot on the Berkeley, Star of India, Surprise, or the B-39 submarine to enjoy the multiple fireworks shows on San Diego Bay. This annual event is hosted by the devoted volunteers of the Star of India Auxiliary to benefit the Maritime Museum of San Diego. The event is always a sell-out and huge success as the BBQ is delicious and its one of the best locations to view the multiple fireworks displays on San Diego Bay.

name: Dressing the Part:  Costume Design at the Old Globe Theatre
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: San Diego History Center teams up with the Old Globe Theatre for a dynamic and engaging exhibition that highlights the entire costume design process for main stage productions.  Guests will see first-hand through video footage, sketch books, fabric swatches, dress forms, etc. how the vision of costume designers comes to fruition in final costume pieces on stage.  Hands-on activities invite guests to try on real costumes made by the Old Globe Costume Shop, as well as to bring those costumes to life by acting out their own created scenes on our interactive stage.  This exhibition commemorates the 75th anniversary of the Old Globe Theatre.

name: History for Half Pints
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: Children, ages 3 to 6, and a favorite adult of their choosing are invited to share some fun-filled, hands-on adventures, which will connect them to the important people, places, and events that have shaped San Diego’s history. Each "History for Half Pints" program includes a story time, an outdoor experience (weather permitting), interactive play and a craft project which can be taken home.  Children must be accompanied by an adult during each program.

Workshops are on Saturdays, Nov. 13, 27, Dec. 18, 2010 and January 15, Feb. 19, and March 19, 2011.  12:30pm - 1:30pm

name: Jane Austen's Emma: A Musical Romantic Comedy
description: Emma, a beautiful and clever young woman who prides herself on her matchmaking ability, is preoccupied with romance yet is clueless to her own feelings of love. When she takes on a young friend as her latest project, her well-intentioned efforts misfire, leading to a whirlwind of complications. Deliciously charming, this new romantic comedy, from Tony Award nominated composer Paul Gordon and directed by Tony Award nominee Jeff Calhoun, brings Jane Austen's masterpiece to musical life.

name: Death of a Salesman
description: After a lifetime as a traveling salesman, Willy Loman finds himself at the end of his career and at the end of his rope. As dreams of the past collide with visions of what might have been, Willy's wife and sons wage a desperate struggle to engage him in the present. The Old Globe's acclaimed "Classics Up Close" series continues with one of the greatest achievements of the 20th century.

description:

name: Whale Watching with San Diego Natural History Museum
description: Whale and Dolphin watching on Hornblower is a once in a lifetime experience in San Diego. Enjoy narration from Captains and Naturalists trained by the San Diego Natural History Museum. You'll get a free tour of north San Diego and see the sea lions that live below the lighthouse at Point Loma. Then you'll reach the open sea and find pods of gray whales, including mothers and calves! You may see hundreds of Common, Pacific White-sided or Risso's Dolphins, plus other sea life and marine birds indigenous to Southern California. This is the prime time season to see whales! This is one of the most fun and interesting trips on Hornblower with a whale exhibit onboard which includes fossils, a presentation by the naturalists, and a movie, called Ocean Oasis, playing on the big screen. Watch whales on the most comfortable and fastest yacht on San Diego Bay. Call 619-686-8715, www.hornblower.com/whales

name: "East Meets West" - The Stillpoint Paintings
venue: Japanese Friendship Garden of San Diego
description:
“East Meets West”
The Stillpoint Paintings by John Diamond, M.D.

Now on display until February 28

Currently featured at the Japanese Friendship Garden’s Exhibit Hall are the powerful, yet graceful collection of Stillpoint paintings done with oriental black ink and acrylics on various mediums by renowned holistic healer and bestselling author John Diamond, M.D.

Life Energy Art represents a new philosophy in the Arts – paintings which are done with the intention of being therapeutic for those viewing them. Inspired by ancient tradition and modern freedom of expression, these works of Action Meditation will move you with their beauty and guide you to find the healing power within. His Haiku paintings are not art, but a source of healing.

Biography
Dr. John Diamond, Artist, Painter, Photographer, and Healer, is a pioneering figure in alternative and holistic medicine. He is the founder of the Arts-Health Institute and the Institute for Life Energy and Creativity; the summation of his work has been drawn together in a major healing system called the Diamond Path of Life. In addition, he is author of over twenty books, including two books on art and creativity and two bestsellers.

description: Migrating grey whales  travel south along our coastline to the waters off Baja California to breed and then back to their summer feeding grounds.  Newport Landing Whale Watching offers cruises daily with  96% success rate.

description: Welcome to Chinquapin, Louisiana, by way of Truvy Jones’ hair salon. One of the most popular American plays of the last century, Steel Magnolias is hilarious, wise and moving, a perfect fit for San Diego’s award-winning ensemble theatre.

name: Nova Intimately
description:
Orchestra Nova shares its intimate side with you through a theme of love.

From the passion of Debussy’s famous sensual tone poem to the heart-rendering beauty of the melodic Transfigured Night and the gentle Christmas gift of devotion with Siegfried Idyll, this is an unforgettable evening of romance and emotion.

Topping off an evening of beautiful music is featured soloist Maria Lozano, winner of Orchestra Nova’s ground-breaking The Next Star talent competition in March 2010. She will sing a beautiful composition depicting a fusion of Bach and Latin American folk music for voice and orchestra from the most renowned Latin American composer of the 20th century.

name: Dee Dee Bridgewater sings Billie Holiday- LJMS Jazz Series
description:
Few entertainers have ever commanded such depth of artistry in every medium. Fewer still have been rewarded with Broadway’s coveted Tony Award, nominated for the London Theater’s West End equivalent, the Laurence Oliver Award, won two Grammy® Awards, and France’s 1998 top honor Victoire de la Musique. Over the course of a multifaceted career that has spanned four decades, Dee Dee Bridgewater has risen to the top tier of today’s jazz vocalists, putting her own unique spin on standards as well as taking intrepid leaps of faith in re-envisioning jazz classics.

You'll get a free tour of north San Diego and see the sea lions that live below the lighthouse at Point Loma. Then you'll reach the open sea and find pods of gray whales, including mothers and calves! You may see hundreds of Common, Pacific White-sided or Risso's Dolphins, plus other sea life and marine birds indigenous to Southern California. This is the prime time season to see whales! This is one of the most fun and interesting trips on Hornblower with a whale exhibit onboard which includes fossils, a presentation by the naturalists, and a movie, called Ocean Oasis, playing on the big screen. Watch whales on the most comfortable and fastest yacht on San Diego Bay. Call 619-686-8715, www.hornblower.com/whales

name: Home Bodies: Selections from the Collection
venue: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, Downtown
description: Home Bodies presents 23 artworks from the Museum’s collection, including paintings, sculpture, prints, and room-sized installations. The exhibition features Pop works by Claes Oldenberg and Joe Goode, dramatic sculptures by Cornelia Parker and Martin Kersels, as well as works by San Diego-based artists Jean Lowe and Manny Farber.  The title playfully suggests the focus of the works on view: one half of the Museum’s 1001 Kettner galleries features art that makes reference to the human body, while the other portion showcases works with domestic images. Home and bodies.

name: World Religions in our San Diego Community - Exhibit Opening
description: Escondido Children’s Museum (ECM) is launching a new, interactive exhibit celebrating World Religions in San Diego on Saturday, December 11, 2010 from 11:00-4:00pm with refreshments from 11:00-12:00 and special programming from 12:00-4:00pm. “World Religions in our San Diego Community” is a hands-on exhibit with special programs intended to promote cultural and religious awareness and understanding.  Programs correlate with many religious holidays, World Religion Day and New Year festivities, while also highlighting celebrations throughout the year. Participating faith communities include Jewish, Hindu, Catholic, Muslim, Buddhist, Baha’I, Mormon and Sikh.

name: Zandra Rhodes -- A Lifelong Love Affair with Textiles
description: Since the 1960s, this internationally renowned British designer, who lives and works half the year in the San Diego area, has been creating imaginative, colorful fabrics and clothing. This retrospective will present her textiles as well as high fashion garments she has created. Rhodes will also select textiles or objects from a number of the cultures represented in Mingei International’s collection to display alongside her work, initiating a lively conversation about influences and inspirations. The exhibition has previously been seen in London, Italy, Australia, and Mexico City.

name: Creating an Artistic Basis:  Local Artists Groups from the Early 20th Century
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: Entering the 20th century, the City of San Diego experienced tremendous growth and development.   In a time of population increase and economic diversification, local artists groups began to shine.  Join us for a look at the work of four unique groups of local artists that helped shape San Diego's artistic identity during the first half of the 20th century.  All artworks on view are from the vast holdings of the San Diego Fine Art Collection.

name: Grandparents & Me:  Theatre Workshops
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: San Diego Junior Theatre and San Diego History Center pair up for a fun, interactive program that engages guests in the creativity of theatre.  In this series of workshops, learn how make-up transforms a person into a "character"; how movement and body language act out a scene without words; or how costumes add dimension and depth to any theatrical performance.  Workshops are on Saturdays, Nov. 13, 27, Dec. 18, 2010 and January 15, Feb. 19, and March 19, 2011.  12:30pm - 1:30pm

name: Counter Cultures: The Secret Lives of Games
description: See over a hundred different board, card, and tile games from all over the world. Learn about the history of games and why we love to play them so much. Step onto a floor-sized game board and travel along spaces that take you through the exhibit! Or rest your feet in our players lounge and play some of your favorite boardgames.

name: Dressing the Part:  Costume Design at the Old Globe Theatre
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: San Diego History Center teams up with the Old Globe Theatre for a dynamic and engaging exhibition that highlights the entire costume design process for main stage productions.  Guests will see first-hand through video footage, sketch books, fabric swatches, dress forms, etc. how the vision of costume designers comes to fruition in final costume pieces on stage.  Hands-on activities invite guests to try on real costumes made by the Old Globe Costume Shop, as well as to bring those costumes to life by acting out their own created scenes on our interactive stage.  This exhibition commemorates the 75th anniversary of the Old Globe Theatre.

name: 18th Annual Sea Chantey Festival
description: For centuries, sailor's have honed their shipboard skills to the cadence of songs recounting the adventure, tragedy and romance of life at sea. These "sea chanteys" come to life in a dramatic way on board the majestic sailing ship Star of India.  The Maritime Museum of San Diego, along with San Diego Folk Heritage, presents the 18th Annual Sea Chantey Fest. This year's lineup TBD

name: Strange Bones: Curiosities of the Human Skeleton
description: This exhibition will focus on the many different strange, odd, and curious things that happen to our skeletons.  In addition to information on bone remodeling and adaptation, examples of skeletal congenital anomalies, diseases that disfigure the skeleton, strange healing patterns of traumatic injuries, and cultural modification of the skeleton and teeth will be highlighted.  This exhibition will scientifically focus on how the human skeleton is extremely interesting and adaptable, and will teach our visitors about the biological forces behind certain skeletal diseases and disfiguration.

name: History for Half Pints
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: Children, ages 3 to 6, and a favorite adult of their choosing are invited to share some fun-filled, hands-on adventures, which will connect them to the important people, places, and events that have shaped San Diego’s history. Each "History for Half Pints" program includes a story time, an outdoor experience (weather permitting), interactive play and a craft project which can be taken home.  Children must be accompanied by an adult during each program.

venue: Coronado Visitor Center and Historical Association & Museum
description:

$10 each; children under twelve are free.

name: Hotel del Coronado Historic Walking Tour
venue: Coronado Visitor Center and Historical Association & Museum
description:
Enjoy the beauty of the Hotel del Coronado, and learn the story of how it came to be built in 1887 on what was then a barren island.

Docents of the Coronado Museum of History and Art lead tours on Tuesdays and Fridays at 10:30 am, and on Saturdays and Sundays at 2:00 pm.

Reservations are required at 619.437.8788. $15 per person; children under twelve are free. Private group tours may be arranged at 619.437.8788.

name: Botanicals: The Photography of Imogen Cunningham
description: A pioneer of 20th century photography, Imogen Cunningham (1883-1976) played a pivotal role in the acceptance of the medium as an art form and the growth of modernism. She began pursuing photography in 1901 and throughout her long career, maintained an interest in portraiture and nature. Unlike other members of the Western School of Photography who also emphasized nature, such as Edward Weston (1886-1958) and Ansel Adams (1902-84), Cunningham created intimate compositions which call attention to the abstract qualities of nature. This exhibition will feature her black and white botanical photographs from the 1920s-1930s. A preview reception introduces the exhibition on Saturday, January 8, 2011 from 5:00 – 7:00 p.m. Admission at the door is $10 and free for OMA members.

name: "East Meets West" - The Stillpoint Paintings
venue: Japanese Friendship Garden of San Diego
description:
“East Meets West”
The Stillpoint Paintings by John Diamond, M.D.

Now on display until February 28

Currently featured at the Japanese Friendship Garden’s Exhibit Hall are the powerful, yet graceful collection of Stillpoint paintings done with oriental black ink and acrylics on various mediums by renowned holistic healer and bestselling author John Diamond, M.D.

Life Energy Art represents a new philosophy in the Arts – paintings which are done with the intention of being therapeutic for those viewing them. Inspired by ancient tradition and modern freedom of expression, these works of Action Meditation will move you with their beauty and guide you to find the healing power within. His Haiku paintings are not art, but a source of healing.

Biography
Dr. John Diamond, Artist, Painter, Photographer, and Healer, is a pioneering figure in alternative and holistic medicine. He is the founder of the Arts-Health Institute and the Institute for Life Energy and Creativity; the summation of his work has been drawn together in a major healing system called the Diamond Path of Life. In addition, he is author of over twenty books, including two books on art and creativity and two bestsellers.

name: Little Miss Sunshine
description: The Hoover family has seen better days. Richard, the father, is a floundering motivational speaker, Grandpa’s been kicked out of his retirement home, and Uncle Frank’s been dumped by his boyfriend. Moody teenager Dwayne has taken a vow of silence and overextended mom Sheryl can do little more than slap on a smile. But when the youngest Hoover… umm, energetic Olive, enters a regional children’s beauty pageant, the family thinks their luck could change and embarks on a cross-country trek chasing the coveted title of “Little Miss Sunshine.”

name: Beats Antique
description: Beats Antique combines the sounds of the Middle East with the styles of hip-hop, brass band, downtempo, glitch and dubstep in a new collage of music that is mixed and broken down with clever breakbeats for an adept international flair. Beats Antique is producing an un-charted style of music by adding live horns, accordion, glockenspiel, viola, string quartets, kalimba, clarinet and various unusual instruments to their big beat arrangements.

name: Fair Use
description: Sexual politics collide with legal brinksmanship in this whip-smart romantic comedy. While attorneys at a Chicago law firm take on a high-profile plagiarism case, their after-hours romantic triangle echoes Cyrano de Bergerac. “The play savors the pleasures of language, sensuality and rich debate over such elusive concepts as intellectual property.” – Creative Loafing/Atlanta, Top 10 Plays of 2009

name: miXtape
description: Take a seriously wild musical ride back to the most awesome of decades.  Reagan was in the White House, Michael Jackson was at the top of the charts, lycra and legwarmers were the accessories du jour, and a “mix tape” of favorite tunes was the ultimate in self-expression.  The lousy economy was about to bounce back like we’d never seen, set to the synthesized beat of 80s Rock.  The Cold War was heating up, and with fingers on the nuclear button, the world was sure to end any moment.  But for Generation X, life was just beginning.  Put on your suspenders, pull out the Members Only jacket, do your hair up with a scrunchy, and “everybody cut footloose” with us in this totally rad musical world premiere. Dress up on Friday nights and get a free beverage of your choice.

name: Art of Elan Season 4: One Voice
description:
For the past 3 years, Art of Élan has been filling the San Diego Museum of Art’s Hibben Gallery with adventurous music lovers in search of an innovative approach to classical music. Led by San Diego Symphony musicians Kate Hatmaker and Demarre McGill, Art of Élan has not disappointed. Their creative one-hour programming has helped break down barriers that surround classical music. The five concert 2010-11 Season promises to continue to engage and energize audiences under the heading of “One Voice."

See website for more info. Concert dates are: Oct 19, Nov 30, Jan 18, March 8 and May 3. All at 7 pm at San Diego Museum of Art

name: John David Ratajkowski:  Portraits of Jewish Literary Figures
description:
The Gotthelf Art Gallery, part of the San Diego Center for Jewish Culture at the Lawrence Family Jewish Community Center, Jacobs Family Campus, is pleased to announce the solo exhibition John David Ratajkowski – From Page to Stage: Portraits of Jewish Literary Figures in Film, running December 8, 2010 – February 23, 2011. Art is for sale, with all proceeds benefiting the artist and the Gotthelf Art Gallery.

An opening night reception with the artist will be held on Wednesday, December 8th at 7:30 p.m. The reception is free and open to the public .

The history of the Jewish figure in American cinema is rich and evocative. Particularly outstanding have been films based on Jewish characters from literature. It is these literary characters translated to film that artist John David Ratajkowski takes as the subject for his series of portraits.

John David Ratajkowski Growing up in the 1950’s in the seaside town of Coronado, California, painter John David Ratajkowski remembers “being able to draw anything I could see.” Fascinated as a boy by all variety of materials, Ratajkowski was early on adept at painting, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, lithography. He recalls that the key attraction for him in every case was the compelling desire “to make”—whatever the media.
Ratajkowski’s experiments in abstract work have powerfully impacted his portraiture. The current series of portraits of Jewish literary figures depicted in film brings together Ratajkowski’s abstract painting techniques with his long-time work in the portrait. Ratajkowski’s work appears in private and corporate collections; he is represented by the Blue Leaf Gallery in Dublin, Ireland, and the CJ Gallery in San Diego, California.

Reagan was in the White House, Michael Jackson was at the top of the charts, lycra and legwarmers were the accessories du jour, and a “mix tape” of favorite tunes was the ultimate in self-expression.  The lousy economy was about to bounce back like we’d never seen, set to the synthesized beat of 80s Rock.  The Cold War was heating up, and with fingers on the nuclear button, the world was sure to end any moment.  But for Generation X, life was just beginning.  Put on your suspenders, pull out the Members Only jacket, do your hair up with a scrunchy, and “everybody cut footloose” with us in this totally rad musical world premiere. Dress up on Friday nights and get a free beverage of your choice.

name: "East Meets West" - The Stillpoint Paintings
venue: Japanese Friendship Garden of San Diego
description:
“East Meets West”
The Stillpoint Paintings by John Diamond, M.D.

Now on display until February 28

Currently featured at the Japanese Friendship Garden’s Exhibit Hall are the powerful, yet graceful collection of Stillpoint paintings done with oriental black ink and acrylics on various mediums by renowned holistic healer and bestselling author John Diamond, M.D.

Life Energy Art represents a new philosophy in the Arts – paintings which are done with the intention of being therapeutic for those viewing them. Inspired by ancient tradition and modern freedom of expression, these works of Action Meditation will move you with their beauty and guide you to find the healing power within. His Haiku paintings are not art, but a source of healing.

Biography
Dr. John Diamond, Artist, Painter, Photographer, and Healer, is a pioneering figure in alternative and holistic medicine. He is the founder of the Arts-Health Institute and the Institute for Life Energy and Creativity; the summation of his work has been drawn together in a major healing system called the Diamond Path of Life. In addition, he is author of over twenty books, including two books on art and creativity and two bestsellers.

name: Southern California Gray Whale Migration 2010/2011
venue: A Whale Adventure-Newport Landing Whale Watching
description: Migrating grey whales  travel south along our coastline to the waters off Baja California to breed and then back to their summer feeding grounds.  Newport Landing Whale Watching offers cruises daily with  96% success rate.

name: Whale Watching with San Diego Natural History Museum
description: Whale and Dolphin watching on Hornblower is a once in a lifetime experience in San Diego. Enjoy narration from Captains and Naturalists trained by the San Diego Natural History Museum. You'll get a free tour of north San Diego and see the sea lions that live below the lighthouse at Point Loma. Then you'll reach the open sea and find pods of gray whales, including mothers and calves! You may see hundreds of Common, Pacific White-sided or Risso's Dolphins, plus other sea life and marine birds indigenous to Southern California. This is the prime time season to see whales! This is one of the most fun and interesting trips on Hornblower with a whale exhibit onboard which includes fossils, a presentation by the naturalists, and a movie, called Ocean Oasis, playing on the big screen. Watch whales on the most comfortable and fastest yacht on San Diego Bay. Call 619-686-8715, www.hornblower.com/whales

name: Art of Elan Season 4: One Voice
description:

Led by San Diego Symphony musicians Kate Hatmaker and Demarre McGill, Art of Élan has not disappointed. The five concert 2010-11 Season promises to continue to engage and energize audiences under the heading of “One Voice."

See website for more info. Concert dates are: Oct 19, Nov 30, Jan 18, March 8 and May 3. All at 7 pm at San Diego Museum of Art

name: World Religions in our San Diego Community - Exhibit Opening
description: Escondido Children’s Museum (ECM) is launching a new, interactive exhibit celebrating World Religions in San Diego on Saturday, December 11, 2010 from 11:00-4:00pm with refreshments from 11:00-12:00 and special programming from 12:00-4:00pm. “World Religions in our San Diego Community” is a hands-on exhibit with special programs intended to promote cultural and religious awareness and understanding.  Programs correlate with many religious holidays, World Religion Day and New Year festivities, while also highlighting celebrations throughout the year. Participating faith communities include Jewish, Hindu, Catholic, Muslim, Buddhist, Baha’I, Mormon and Sikh.

name: Zandra Rhodes -- A Lifelong Love Affair with Textiles
description: Since the 1960s, this internationally renowned British designer, who lives and works half the year in the San Diego area, has been creating imaginative, colorful fabrics and clothing. This retrospective will present her textiles as well as high fashion garments she has created. Rhodes will also select textiles or objects from a number of the cultures represented in Mingei International’s collection to display alongside her work, initiating a lively conversation about influences and inspirations. The exhibition has previously been seen in London, Italy, Australia, and Mexico City.

name: Creating an Artistic Basis:  Local Artists Groups from the Early 20th Century
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: Entering the 20th century, the City of San Diego experienced tremendous growth and development.   In a time of population increase and economic diversification, local artists groups began to shine.  Join us for a look at the work of four unique groups of local artists that helped shape San Diego's artistic identity during the first half of the 20th century.  All artworks on view are from the vast holdings of the San Diego Fine Art Collection.

name: Grandparents & Me:  Theatre Workshops
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: San Diego Junior Theatre and San Diego History Center pair up for a fun, interactive program that engages guests in the creativity of theatre.  In this series of workshops, learn how make-up transforms a person into a "character"; how movement and body language act out a scene without words; or how costumes add dimension and depth to any theatrical performance.  Workshops are on Saturdays, Nov. 13, 27, Dec. 18, 2010 and January 15, Feb. 19, and March 19, 2011.  12:30pm - 1:30pm

name: Counter Cultures: The Secret Lives of Games
description: See over a hundred different board, card, and tile games from all over the world. Learn about the history of games and why we love to play them so much. Step onto a floor-sized game board and travel along spaces that take you through the exhibit! Or rest your feet in our players lounge and play some of your favorite boardgames.

name: Dressing the Part:  Costume Design at the Old Globe Theatre
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: San Diego History Center teams up with the Old Globe Theatre for a dynamic and engaging exhibition that highlights the entire costume design process for main stage productions.  Guests will see first-hand through video footage, sketch books, fabric swatches, dress forms, etc. how the vision of costume designers comes to fruition in final costume pieces on stage.  Hands-on activities invite guests to try on real costumes made by the Old Globe Costume Shop, as well as to bring those costumes to life by acting out their own created scenes on our interactive stage.  This exhibition commemorates the 75th anniversary of the Old Globe Theatre.

name: Botanicals: The Photography of Imogen Cunningham
description: A pioneer of 20th century photography, Imogen Cunningham (1883-1976) played a pivotal role in the acceptance of the medium as an art form and the growth of modernism. She began pursuing photography in 1901 and throughout her long career, maintained an interest in portraiture and nature. Unlike other members of the Western School of Photography who also emphasized nature, such as Edward Weston (1886-1958) and Ansel Adams (1902-84), Cunningham created intimate compositions which call attention to the abstract qualities of nature. This exhibition will feature her black and white botanical photographs from the 1920s-1930s. A preview reception introduces the exhibition on Saturday, January 8, 2011 from 5:00 – 7:00 p.m. Admission at the door is $10 and free for OMA members.

name: 18th Annual Sea Chantey Festival
description: For centuries, sailor's have honed their shipboard skills to the cadence of songs recounting the adventure, tragedy and romance of life at sea. These "sea chanteys" come to life in a dramatic way on board the majestic sailing ship Star of India.  The Maritime Museum of San Diego, along with San Diego Folk Heritage, presents the 18th Annual Sea Chantey Fest. This year's lineup TBD

name: Home Bodies: Selections from the Collection
venue: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, Downtown
description: Home Bodies presents 23 artworks from the Museum’s collection, including paintings, sculpture, prints, and room-sized installations. The exhibition features Pop works by Claes Oldenberg and Joe Goode, dramatic sculptures by Cornelia Parker and Martin Kersels, as well as works by San Diego-based artists Jean Lowe and Manny Farber. The title playfully suggests the focus of the works on view: one half of the Museum’s 1001 Kettner galleries features art that makes reference to the human body, while the other portion showcases works with domestic images. Home and bodies.

name: Strange Bones: Curiosities of the Human Skeleton
description: This exhibition will focus on the many different strange, odd, and curious things that happen to our skeletons.  In addition to information on bone remodeling and adaptation, examples of skeletal congenital anomalies, diseases that disfigure the skeleton, strange healing patterns of traumatic injuries, and cultural modification of the skeleton and teeth will be highlighted.  This exhibition will scientifically focus on how the human skeleton is extremely interesting and adaptable, and will teach our visitors about the biological forces behind certain skeletal diseases and disfiguration.

name: History for Half Pints
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: Children, ages 3 to 6, and a favorite adult of their choosing are invited to share some fun-filled, hands-on adventures, which will connect them to the important people, places, and events that have shaped San Diego’s history. Each "History for Half Pints" program includes a story time, an outdoor experience (weather permitting), interactive play and a craft project which can be taken home.  Children must be accompanied by an adult during each program.

name: Coronado Heritage Walk
venue: Coronado Visitor Center and Historical Association & Museum
description:
Start in the Museum of History and Art, and then proceed along historic Orange Avenue, through the neighborhoods of Coronado's grand homes, and to the beautiful Hotel del Coronado. Docents from the Coronado Historical Association relate the story of how Coronado was settled and became the gem that it is today.

Tours are Wednesdays at 10:30 am. Reservations are required at 619.437.8788. Private group tours may be arranged at 619.437-8788.

$10 each; children under twelve are free.

name: Hotel del Coronado Historic Walking Tour
venue: Coronado Visitor Center and Historical Association & Museum
description:
Enjoy the beauty of the Hotel del Coronado, and learn the story of how it came to be built in 1887 on what was then a barren island.

Docents of the Coronado Museum of History and Art lead tours on Tuesdays and Fridays at 10:30 am, and on Saturdays and Sundays at 2:00 pm.

Reservations are required at 619.437.8788. $15 per person; children under twelve are free. Private group tours may be arranged at 619.437.8788.

name: John David Ratajkowski:  Portraits of Jewish Literary Figures
description:
The Gotthelf Art Gallery, part of the San Diego Center for Jewish Culture at the Lawrence Family Jewish Community Center, Jacobs Family Campus, is pleased to announce the solo exhibition John David Ratajkowski – From Page to Stage: Portraits of Jewish Literary Figures in Film, running December 8, 2010 – February 23, 2011. Art is for sale, with all proceeds benefiting the artist and the Gotthelf Art Gallery.

An opening night reception with the artist will be held on Wednesday, December 8th at 7:30 p.m. The reception is free and open to the public .

The history of the Jewish figure in American cinema is rich and evocative. Particularly outstanding have been films based on Jewish characters from literature. It is these literary characters translated to film that artist John David Ratajkowski takes as the subject for his series of portraits.

John David Ratajkowski Growing up in the 1950’s in the seaside town of Coronado, California, painter John David Ratajkowski remembers “being able to draw anything I could see.” Fascinated as a boy by all variety of materials, Ratajkowski was early on adept at painting, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, lithography. He recalls that the key attraction for him in every case was the compelling desire “to make”—whatever the media.
Ratajkowski’s experiments in abstract work have powerfully impacted his portraiture. The current series of portraits of Jewish literary figures depicted in film brings together Ratajkowski’s abstract painting techniques with his long-time work in the portrait. Ratajkowski’s work appears in private and corporate collections; he is represented by the Blue Leaf Gallery in Dublin, Ireland, and the CJ Gallery in San Diego, California.

name: Intimate Whale Watching Tours Without the Crowds
description:
Whale Watching with Sail San Diego is incredible experience, where the groups are small, and our experienced Captains/Trained Naturalists are the best in the business!

This is a great trip and experience for all ages! We are very conscious of our environment and carefully follow the rules of whale watching and have a huge respect for these magnificent mammals and the journey they are on! We run environmentally responsible trips, something we feel is so important.

Because we run small groups on one of our two beautiful 40’ Catalina's, you and your guests and family can have an intimate time on the water and have all your questions about the grey whale and the whale migration answered by our knowledgeable Trained Naturalists who have a wealth of information and love to share all they know with our guests. We also keep whale watching literature on the boats that is easy and fun to read. Not sitting on a microphone far away from guests, our Captains are right there to help you experience nature at its best. The Captains who are in arms reach look for Whales, Dolphins, Porpoise, Sea Lions and Pelagic Sea Birds. Captains will tell you about the plant-life and actually do a hands-on demo for kids and show them all the signs to look out for while looking for whales or dolphins. Not only is this trip informative it is FUN!!

Last year there were very few trips where no whales were spotted but we always guarantee sea lions! We will work with you on a second trip if no whales are spotted- most of the time this is not the case! Whale Watching trips are scheduled twice a day. We do a morning whale watching trip and a mid-day whale watching trip. Times vary because we know some of our guests are here on business and have schedules and itinerary’s to keep. Call us for times and details.

All the trips offer complimentary beverages which include beer/wine, non-alcoholic beverages and nice hot-chocolate for those chilly days! Snacks are also provided for guest to enjoy while under way. To ensure the comfort of each guest we also provide extra jackets, blankets, foul-weather gear, hats, gloves, sunscreens, for those who forget – sunglasses. All of this is there for our guests to enjoy and we encourage everyone to be as comfortable as possible. Enjoy the whale watching literature on the boats, sit back, relax and enjoy the most memorable time on the water possible.

description:
Winter Pops Special Concert
Russ Peck, organ

Performing his own stunts, master silent comedian Harold Lloyd is the new office boy who finds himself famously clinging to a towering clock-face just to keep his job! The performance begins at 8:00 P.M.

San Diego Symphony does not perform on this special screening event.

For ticketing and more information, go here: http://www.sandiegosymphony.org/calendar/view.aspx?id=2213

name: Mike Pinto with Shoreline Rootz, Tribal Theory and Megan Combs
description: For the last eight years, Mike Pinto has crafted an exceptional style of songwriting, with truly unique rhymes that raise the bar in today’s music. Pinto’s sound blends Reggae, Ska, Surf, and even Latin rhythms, but it’s his distinct voice and seamless storytelling that has brought him success in the U.S. and abroad.

name: San Diego Museum Month: Half-Off Admission
description:
During February, pick up a free Museum Month Pass at San Diego area Macy's and you (plus 3 guests) will receive half-off admission at 40 of San Diego County's greatest museums! From ancient history to futuristic technology, from sublime art to childlike curiosity, families, couples and experts alike will find museums that are as affordable as they are thrilling. Welcome to "Entertainment that has value".

Museum Month features some of San Diego's greatest points of interest:

  • Adobe Chapel Museum
  • Barona Cultural Center & Museum
  • Birch Aquarium at Scripps
  • Bonita Museum & Cultural Center
  • California Center for the Arts, Museum (Feb. 12-28)
  • Coronado Museum of History & Art
  • Escondido Children's Museum
  • Flying Leatherneck Aviation Museum
  • Heritage of the Americas Museum

name: World Religions in our San Diego Community - Exhibit Opening
description: Escondido Children’s Museum (ECM) is launching a new, interactive exhibit celebrating World Religions in San Diego on Saturday, December 11, 2010 from 11:00-4:00pm with refreshments from 11:00-12:00 and special programming from 12:00-4:00pm. “World Religions in our San Diego Community” is a hands-on exhibit with special programs intended to promote cultural and religious awareness and understanding.  Programs correlate with many religious holidays, World Religion Day and New Year festivities, while also highlighting celebrations throughout the year. Participating faith communities include Jewish, Hindu, Catholic, Muslim, Buddhist, Baha’I, Mormon and Sikh.

name: Zandra Rhodes -- A Lifelong Love Affair with Textiles
description: Since the 1960s, this internationally renowned British designer, who lives and works half the year in the San Diego area, has been creating imaginative, colorful fabrics and clothing. This retrospective will present her textiles as well as high fashion garments she has created. Rhodes will also select textiles or objects from a number of the cultures represented in Mingei International’s collection to display alongside her work, initiating a lively conversation about influences and inspirations. The exhibition has previously been seen in London, Italy, Australia, and Mexico City.

name: Creating an Artistic Basis:  Local Artists Groups from the Early 20th Century
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: Entering the 20th century, the City of San Diego experienced tremendous growth and development.   In a time of population increase and economic diversification, local artists groups began to shine.  Join us for a look at the work of four unique groups of local artists that helped shape San Diego's artistic identity during the first half of the 20th century.  All artworks on view are from the vast holdings of the San Diego Fine Art Collection.

name: Grandparents & Me:  Theatre Workshops
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: San Diego Junior Theatre and San Diego History Center pair up for a fun, interactive program that engages guests in the creativity of theatre.  In this series of workshops, learn how make-up transforms a person into a "character"; how movement and body language act out a scene without words; or how costumes add dimension and depth to any theatrical performance.  Workshops are on Saturdays, Nov. 13, 27, Dec. 18, 2010 and January 15, Feb. 19, and March 19, 2011.  12:30pm - 1:30pm

name: Counter Cultures: The Secret Lives of Games
description: See over a hundred different board, card, and tile games from all over the world. Learn about the history of games and why we love to play them so much. Step onto a floor-sized game board and travel along spaces that take you through the exhibit! Or rest your feet in our players lounge and play some of your favorite boardgames.

name: Dressing the Part:  Costume Design at the Old Globe Theatre
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: San Diego History Center teams up with the Old Globe Theatre for a dynamic and engaging exhibition that highlights the entire costume design process for main stage productions.  Guests will see first-hand through video footage, sketch books, fabric swatches, dress forms, etc. how the vision of costume designers comes to fruition in final costume pieces on stage.  Hands-on activities invite guests to try on real costumes made by the Old Globe Costume Shop, as well as to bring those costumes to life by acting out their own created scenes on our interactive stage.  This exhibition commemorates the 75th anniversary of the Old Globe Theatre.

name: Botanicals: The Photography of Imogen Cunningham
description: A pioneer of 20th century photography, Imogen Cunningham (1883-1976) played a pivotal role in the acceptance of the medium as an art form and the growth of modernism. She began pursuing photography in 1901 and throughout her long career, maintained an interest in portraiture and nature. Unlike other members of the Western School of Photography who also emphasized nature, such as Edward Weston (1886-1958) and Ansel Adams (1902-84), Cunningham created intimate compositions which call attention to the abstract qualities of nature. This exhibition will feature her black and white botanical photographs from the 1920s-1930s. A preview reception introduces the exhibition on Saturday, January 8, 2011 from 5:00 – 7:00 p.m. Admission at the door is $10 and free for OMA members.

name: 18th Annual Sea Chantey Festival
description: For centuries, sailor's have honed their shipboard skills to the cadence of songs recounting the adventure, tragedy and romance of life at sea. These "sea chanteys" come to life in a dramatic way on board the majestic sailing ship Star of India.  The Maritime Museum of San Diego, along with San Diego Folk Heritage, presents the 18th Annual Sea Chantey Fest. This year's lineup TBD

name: Home Bodies: Selections from the Collection
venue: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, Downtown
description: Home Bodies presents 23 artworks from the Museum’s collection, including paintings, sculpture, prints, and room-sized installations. The exhibition features Pop works by Claes Oldenberg and Joe Goode, dramatic sculptures by Cornelia Parker and Martin Kersels, as well as works by San Diego-based artists Jean Lowe and Manny Farber. The title playfully suggests the focus of the works on view: one half of the Museum’s 1001 Kettner galleries features art that makes reference to the human body, while the other portion showcases works with domestic images. Home and bodies.

name: Strange Bones: Curiosities of the Human Skeleton
description: This exhibition will focus on the many different strange, odd, and curious things that happen to our skeletons.  In addition to information on bone remodeling and adaptation, examples of skeletal congenital anomalies, diseases that disfigure the skeleton, strange healing patterns of traumatic injuries, and cultural modification of the skeleton and teeth will be highlighted.  This exhibition will scientifically focus on how the human skeleton is extremely interesting and adaptable, and will teach our visitors about the biological forces behind certain skeletal diseases and disfiguration.

name: History for Half Pints
venue: Museum of San Diego History and Research Library
description: Children, ages 3 to 6, and a favorite adult of their choosing are invited to share some fun-filled, hands-on adventures, which will connect them to the important people, places, and events that have shaped San Diego’s history. Each "History for Half Pints" program includes a story time, an outdoor experience (weather permitting), interactive play and a craft project which can be taken home.  Children must be accompanied by an adult during each program.

name: Coronado Heritage Walk
venue: Coronado Visitor Center and Historical Association & Museum
description:
Start in the Museum of History and Art, and then proceed along historic Orange Avenue, through the neighborhoods of Coronado's grand homes, and to the beautiful Hotel del Coronado. Docents from the Coronado Historical Association relate the story of how Coronado was settled and became the gem that it is today.

Tours are Wednesdays at 10:30 am. Reservations are required at 619.437.8788. Private group tours may be arranged at 619.437-8788.

$10 each; children under twelve are free.

name: Hotel del Coronado Historic Walking Tour
venue: Coronado Visitor Center and Historical Association & Museum
description:
Enjoy the beauty of the Hotel del Coronado, and learn the story of how it came to be built in 1887 on what was then a barren island.

Docents of the Coronado Museum of History and Art lead tours on Tuesdays and Fridays at 10:30 am, and on Saturdays and Sundays at 2:00 pm.

Reservations are required at 619.437.8788. $15 per person; children under twelve are free. Private group tours may be arranged at 619.437.8788.

name: Wings of Gold: Coronado and Naval Aviation
venue: Coronado Visitor Center and Historical Association & Museum
description: WINGS OF GOLD: CORONADO AND NAVAL AVIATION, at the Coronado Museum of History & Art. Explores naval aviation’s origins 100 years ago in Coronado, forever changing military history. Includes rare photographs, artifacts and video about the heroes and pioneering events that transpired on the Crown Isle. 1100 Orange Ave, Coronado. 619-435-7242.

name: "East Meets West" - The Stillpoint Paintings
venue: Japanese Friendship Garden of San Diego
description:
“East Meets West”
The Stillpoint Paintings by John Diamond, M.D.

Now on display until February 28

Currently featured at the Japanese Friendship Garden’s Exhibit Hall are the powerful, yet graceful collection of Stillpoint paintings done with oriental black ink and acrylics on various mediums by renowned holistic healer and bestselling author John Diamond, M.D.

Life Energy Art represents a new philosophy in the Arts – paintings which are done with the intention of being therapeutic for those viewing them. Inspired by ancient tradition and modern freedom of expression, these works of Action Meditation will move you with their beauty and guide you to find the healing power within. His Haiku paintings are not art, but a source of healing.

Biography
Dr. John Diamond, Artist, Painter, Photographer, and Healer, is a pioneering figure in alternative and holistic medicine. He is the founder of the Arts-Health Institute and the Institute for Life Energy and Creativity; the summation of his work has been drawn together in a major healing system called the Diamond Path of Life. In addition, he is author of over twenty books, including two books on art and creativity and two bestsellers.

name: Southern California Gray Whale Migration 2010/2011
venue: A Whale Adventure-Newport Landing Whale Watching
description: Migrating grey whales  travel south along our coastline to the waters off Baja California to breed and then back to their summer feeding grounds.  Newport Landing Whale Watching offers cruises daily with  96% success rate.

name: Whale Watching with Birch Aquarium Naturalists
description:
Join naturalists from the Birch Aquarium at Scripps aboard Flagship Cruises & Events three-and-a-half hour narrated cruise that includes gray whale artifacts, specimens and a take-home information packet on the gray whale. Binoculars available to rent.

Reservation strongly recommended. Whale sightings guaranteed on all cruises or whale watchers cruise again for free.

Departures: 9:45am & 1:30pm
Cruise last approx. 3 - 3.5 hours

name: Whale Watching with San Diego Natural History Museum
description: Whale and Dolphin watching on Hornblower is a once in a lifetime experience in San Diego. Enjoy narration from Captains and Naturalists trained by the San Diego Natural History Museum. You'll get a free tour of north San Diego and see the sea lions that live below the lighthouse at Point Loma. Then you'll reach the open sea and find pods of gray whales, including mothers and calves! You may see hundreds of Common, Pacific White-sided or Risso's Dolphins, plus other sea life and marine birds indigenous to Southern California. This is the prime time season to see whales! This is one of the most fun and interesting trips on Hornblower with a whale exhibit onboard which includes fossils, a presentation by the naturalists, and a movie, called Ocean Oasis, playing on the big screen. Watch whales on the most comfortable and fastest yacht on San Diego Bay. Call 619-686-8715, www.hornblower.com/whales

name: Intimate Whale Watching Tours Without the Crowds
description:
Whale Watching with Sail San Diego is incredible experience, where the groups are small, and our experienced Captains/Trained Naturalists are the best in the business!

This is a great trip and experience for all ages! We are very conscious of our environment and carefully follow the rules of whale watching and have a huge respect for these magnificent mammals and the journey they are on! We run environmentally responsible trips, something we feel is so important.

Because we run small groups on one of our two beautiful 40’ Catalina's, you and your guests and family can have an intimate time on the water and have all your questions about the grey whale and the whale migration answered by our knowledgeable Trained Naturalists who have a wealth of information and love to share all they know with our guests. We also keep whale watching literature on the boats that is easy and fun to read. Not sitting on a microphone far away from guests, our Captains are right there to help you experience nature at its best. The Captains who are in arms reach look for Whales, Dolphins, Porpoise, Sea Lions and Pelagic Sea Birds. Captains will tell you about the plant-life and actually do a hands-on demo for kids and show them all the signs to look out for while looking for whales or dolphins. Not only is this trip informative it is FUN!!

Last year there were very few trips where no whales were spotted but we always guarantee sea lions! We will work with you on a second trip if no whales are spotted- most of the time this is not the case! Whale Watching trips are scheduled twice a day. We do a morning whale watching trip and a mid-day whale watching trip. Times vary because we know some of our guests are here on business and have schedules and itinerary’s to keep. Call us for times and details.

All the trips offer complimentary beverages which include beer/wine, non-alcoholic beverages and nice hot-chocolate for those chilly days! Snacks are also provided for guest to enjoy while under way. To ensure the comfort of each guest we also provide extra jackets, blankets, foul-weather gear, hats, gloves, sunscreens, for those who forget – sunglasses. All of this is there for our guests to enjoy and we encourage everyone to be as comfortable as possible. Enjoy the whale watching literature on the boats, sit back, relax and enjoy the most memorable time on the water possible.

name: An Evening with Rita Rudner
description:
From Broadway to the comedy clubs of Manhattan, from television to Las Vegas, Rita Rudner is one of the funniest and hard-working comedians in the business today.

Since leaving the stage, where she started as a dancer in Broadway shows, she has progressed from guest appearances on The Tonight Show with Johnny Carson and Late Night with David Letterman to hosting her own HBO award-winning specials.

Ms. Rudner and her producer-husband Martin Bergman, wrote the screenplay of the film Peter's Friends, in which she also acted. She is the author of the best-selling I Still Have It; I Just Can't Remember Where I Put It, Naked Beneath My Clothes and the novels Tickled Pink and Turning The Tables and has written several screenplays with her husband.

Known for her trademark epigrammatic style, she has performed almost exclusively in Las Vegas since 2001, selling over one million tickets and is currently under contract with Harrah's until 2012...so don't miss this rare opportunity to see her perform live in San Diego!

Run Time: tba

Location: Balboa Theatre - 868 Fourth Ave @ E St.

name: Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra
description:
No other musical ensemble is more consistently and closely associated with the history and tradition of European classical music than the Vienna Philharmonic. In the course of its 160 year history, the musicians of this prominent orchestra have been an integral part of a musical epoch which, due to an abundance of uniquely gifted composers and interpreters, must certainly be regarded as unique.
The statements of countless preeminent musical personalities of the past best illustrate the orchestra's close association with this rich musical history. Richard Wagner described the orchestra as being one of the most outstanding in the world and Anton Bruckner called it "the most superior musical association". Gustav Mahler went further still, claiming to be joined together through "the bonds of musical art". Richard Strauss summarized these sentiments by saying: "All praise of the Vienna Philharmonic reveals itself as understatement."

Semyon Bychkov, conductor

SCHUMANN
Symphony No. 2 in C Major, Op. 73

BRAHMS
Symphony No. 2 in D Major, Op. 61

name: Tchaikovsky Spectacular
description: This exciting program includes the timeless beauty of "Swan Lake Act II" that is simply unforgettable, the famous section from the 3rd Act of "Swan Lake" - the "Black Swan Pas de Deux" that is a classical, virtuoso tour-d-force, and Resident Choreographer Elizabeth Wistrich's enchanting and highly entertaining neo-classical ballet to Tchakiovsky's much loved score "The Seasons" depicting the twelve months of the year.

name: Ray Chen, violin- LJMS Discovery Series
description:
Winner of the Queen Elisabeth Competition (2009) and the Yehudi Menuhin Competition (2008), Ray Chen is among the most compelling young violinists today. His recent performances, including debut recitals at the Kennedy Center in Washington D. C. and the Merkin Hall in New York, have enraptured both the audiences and the critics.

name: The Joffrey Ballet- LJMS Dance Series
description: For more than a half-century, the Joffrey Ballet’s commitment to taking world-class, artistically vibrant work to a broad and varied audience has created a solid foundation that continues to support the company’s unprecedented capacity for achieving important “firsts.”  Classically-trained to the highest standards, the Joffrey Ballet expresses a unique, inclusive perspective on dance, proudly reflecting the diversity of America with its company, audiences, and repertoire which includes major story ballets, reconstructions of masterpieces and contemporary works.

Jacobs Masterworks Concert

name: Groundswell
description: In a small lodge on the ferociously rocky coast of South Africa, two men plot to convince their lone guest to invest in their diamond mining scheme. The three men find themselves caught in a power struggle fueled by greed and desperation and will go to any length to secure a chance at a better life. This unforgettable thriller offers a provocative look at a society still haunted by its divided past.

name: An Afternoon in Vienna featuring Opole, Poland Philharmonic
description:
The history of the Opole, Philharmonic of Poland can be traced back to the years immediately following World War II. One of Poland's leading Orchestra's, the Opole, Philharmonic of Poland was founded in 1947 and became the resident Orchestra of Opole. In 1952, a major Performing Arts Center was built in the city of Opole as permanent home to the Orchestra. In June 1969, the Orchestra was awarded by the Ministry of Culture of Poland the State Award for Arts Excellence in honor of the great Polish Composer Josef Eisner.

The Opole, Philharmonic of Poland has performed with the most outstanding piano, violin, and vocal soloists in the world. Since 1960, the Orchestra has participated regularly in prestigious Polish cultural events and travels extensively abroad to countries as far reaching as Spain, France, Holland, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom...and now they're performing in San Diego and will fill the historic Balboa Theatre with the music of their Vienna Gala program.

description:
Chamber Music Series Concert

Acclaimed chamber musician and pianist Orli Shaham performs with members of the San Diego Symphony in a program featuring Mendelssohn’s Piano Trio No. 2 in C minor. The performance begins at 7:30 P.M.

name: André Watts
description:
André Watts burst upon the music world at the age of 16 when Leonard Bernstein chose him to make his debut with the New York Philharmonic in their Young People's Concerts which are broadcast nationwide. Only two weeks later, Maestro Bernstein asked him to be a last minute substitute for the ailing Glenn Gould in performances of Liszt's E-flat Concerto with the New York Philharmonic, thus launching his career in storybook fashion. More than 45 years later, André Watts remains one of today's most celebrated and beloved superstars and performs an all-Liszt program in honor of the Liszt’s Bicentennial Celebration.

name: Les Violons du Roy- Revelle Chamber Music Series
description:
Widely acclaimed for the exceptional energy, brilliance and vitality of its performances, the chamber orchestra Les Violons du Roy borrows its name from the renowned string orchestra of the court of the French kings. The Canadian group, which has a core membership of fifteen players, was brought together in 1984 by music director Bernard Labadie and specializes in the vast repertoire of music for chamber orchestra, performed in the stylistic manner most appropriate to each era. Although the ensemble plays on modern instruments, Les Violons du Roy uses copies of period bows in this repertoire and its approach to the works of the Baroque and Classical periods has been strongly influenced by current research into performance practice in the 17th and early 18th centuries.

8 pm * MCASD Sherwood Auditorium

name: Hal Holbrook's Mark Twain Tonight!
description:
A living, breathing American masterpiece!

The show is, quite simply, one of the most acclaimed and enduring performances in the history of Theatre.

Hal Holbrook took to the stage almost 60 years ago, in a tiny off-Broadway theatre and introduced the world to a man they'd never forget. Winner of the 1966 Tony Award for Best Actor in a Dramatic Role and a 1966 Drama Circle Critic's Award, Mr. Holbrook continues to enthrall audiences around the world with his one-man show.

Mr. Holbrook performed the first show at the Balboa Theatre official re-opening in 2008, selling out the house and thrilling audiences with an incredible evening of Theatre. So whether you come back to see the magic again, or come for the first time, experience a show you'll never forget in the beautiful, historic setting of the Balboa Theatre.

name: Rafta, Rafta...
description: Following their wedding, two newlyweds find that starting their life together under the groom's family’s roof is no honeymoon.  With warmth and humor, this British comedy examines what happens when a young couple must choose between saving money or their marriage.

name: San Diego Symphony: Silent Film Night - Peter Pan
description:
Winter Pops Concert
Gillian Anderson, conductor
Betty Bronson as Peter Pan and Anna May Wong as Tiger Lily

One of the most beautifully, visually innovative films of the Silent Era comes to Symphony Hall with San Diego Symphony as the live soundtrack! Peter Pan, Wendy and her brothers escape to Neverland where they struggle to rescue the Lost Boys from Captain Hook and his band of pirates, encountering along the way the delightful fairy Tinkerbell, a man-eating crocodile, and a band of valiant Indians. Based closely on J. M. Barrie’s original play. The performance starts at 8:00 P.M. on Friday and Saturday.

For more information, go here: http://www.sandiegosymphony.org/calendar/view.aspx?id=2155

name: Brentano String Quartet- Revelle Chamber Music Series
description:
Since its inception in 1992, the Brentano String Quartet has appeared throughout the world to popular and critical acclaim. Within a few years of its formation, the Quartet garnered the first Cleveland Quartet Award and the Naumburg Chamber Music Award, and in 1996 the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center invited them to be the inaugural members of Chamber Music Society Two, a program which was to become a coveted distinction for chamber groups and individuals.

description: The Gallery Series takes place at the Meyer Fine Art Gallery, 2400 Kettner Blvd., #104, in Little Italy.  This series offers the ultimate sensory experience by combining hand-crafted wine, evocative art, and eclectic music.  The evening begins with a curated wine tasting complimented by light hors d'oeuvres.  Following the musical progam, guests are invited to meet the artists.

name: A Touch of the Classics
description:
Classic fairytales come to life through the beauty and splendor of classical ballet. Famous fairytale characters such as Princess Aurora, Puss 'n Boots, and Little Red Riding Hood will share the stage beside the graceful swans of Swan Lake and the daring Pirate Conrad of Les Corsaire! Perfect for children ages four to ninety-seven, A Touch of the Classics tells the tales of Sleeping Beauty, Swan Lake, and Les Corsaire as only ballet can.

Conductor Dana Mambourg Zimbric returns to lead you and your family through an exploration of The ABC's of Musical Literacy at the historic Balboa Theatre.

Children become familiar with the instruments of the orchestra, learn how music is made, and how music comes together in all sorts of ways. This interactive and entertaining season is sure to delight music lovers of all ages.

Joined by guets Jerry Hager and San Diego Pantomime, The Classics Philharmonic will perform the Vivaldi classic!

After the Concert, children and their families are invited on to the stage for Kid's Chat. Members of the orchestra and the conductor are available to sign your program book, answer your questions and smile for your pictures! It's always an enjoyable way to conclude the concert!


Scheduled Program
Vivaldi Four Seasons
