name: The Robert Cray Band
description:
On The Robert Cray Band: Live From Across The Pond, the first release on Cray’s own Nozzle Records imprint, the celebrated triple-threat singer, guitar slinger, and songwriter presents the best moments from his week-long run at London’s Royal Albert Hall in May 2006, opening for friend and mutual admirer Eric Clapton. From classic titles (“Phone Booth”) to highlights from his latest releases (“Poor Johnny”), whether addressing timeless themes of heartache and romance (“The Things You Do To Me”) or this morning’s headlines (“Twenty”), Cray delivers on a promise he’s been making since his first trip into the studio. That promise to record himself and his band when inspired by their fans at the instant of performance pays off on Live. And it pays double, by the way, on two CDs, each packed with about as much intense, emotional playing as a listener can handle in one sitting all of it a pristine reproduction of what transpired under the spotlights, without a single edit or punch-in.

Once the rush of Live begins to settle down, though, it’s natural to wonder why Cray took this long to document his stage chops. Ask him, and his answer is disarmingly candid. “In the past, whenever we’ve known that we were going to record ourselves onstage, we’ve just gotten too psyched up to sound as strong as we normally do,” he says. “You go into it feeling like you’ve got this one shot, and that can be challenging. I’ve actually lost my voice from the anticipation.” Live was different in that it draws from seven consecutive shows at the Royal Albert Hall, which allowed Cray and his road-seasoned band keyboardist Jim Pugh, bassist Karl Sevareid, and drummer Kevin Hayes to feel more at home from one night to the next. “After just a short while we weren’t even thinking about the recording,” he explains. “We were only thinking about the music and about playing at this particular venue.”

Cray and his crew were in fact familiar with the Royal Albert Hall, having played there more than a few times with Clapton over the years. That, plus Cray’s affection for London in general, contributed to the vibe. It’s a paradox, perhaps, that as musicians relax, they lock tighter with each other and play with deeper feeling yet the evidence is there, on each track of Live. When the London dates were done, Cray returned to the States and began going over the results. What he heard was, he admits, an eye-opener in some ways. “When I’m playing up there, I don’t really catch everything that’s going on. But when I sat back and listened to the tapes, it was like, ‘Wow, these guys are great!’” He laughs at his own surprise after all, knowing each player as long as he has, the excellence of these recordings was more a reminder than a revelation. “What I mean is, so much stuff goes on that I can’t really catch it all. I’m singing and feeling their support, but when I take myself out of the playing picture and just listen, that’s when I really hear how magical the ensemble can be.”

The toughest part of putting Live together involved choosing which tracks would make the cut. Cray tackled this job meticulously, playing through all seven concerts and taking detailed notes. “I was listening for the best performances,” he explains. “I listened for enthusiasm, if that’s what was called for in the song. And I listened for things that stood out from the norm. One night, for example, we played ‘Our Last Time,’ and Jim Pugh, who normally plays piano on that one, decided to do it on organ. I went with that version not only because it sounded great but also because it was so uncommon.” Cray’s band rocks and wails and plunges way down to the bottom of the blues well on track after track. And as for Pugh’s solo organ showcase in the midst of “The One in the Middle”? Let’s say that unless you’re going to a sanctified church every Sunday, it’s been a while since you’ve heard anything like this. Aside from their musicianship, the key to Cray and his band is their history. Through more than a thousand gigs played around the world, they’ve locked in a sound that’s elegant and direct, searing and smooth.

And before that, Cray himself developed quickly, having been raised on the gospel and soul records in his parents’ collection while growing up in Georgia and Washington State. By the time he formed his first band in 1974, the components of his sound were in place: a vocal delivery rooted in the Stax/soul tradition and a Stratocaster guitar style that even then stood him out among the greatest of his peers in the blues. Perhaps another reason for the passion of Live owes to the importance of England in helping Cray launch his career. His second album, Bad Influence (1984), shot to number one on the U.K. indie charts while Clapton paid tribute to his colleague by covering the title song. From that point he rose quickly to worldwide prominence, earning his first Grammy for Strong Persuader (1986), releasing one double-platinum and two gold albums, and appearing or recording with the Rolling Stones, B. B. King, Muddy Waters, John Lee Hooker, Chuck Berry, Bonnie Raitt, and other giants.

name: An Evening with Johnny Clegg
description: Johnny Clegg is a singer, songwriter, dancer, anthropologist and musical activist whose music has exploded onto the international scene and broken through barriers in his home of South Africa. Clegg and Sipho Mchunu formed mixed-race Juluka in the late `70s and went on to record two platinum and five gold albums. In 1986 he formed Savuka and by the end of 1989 the band’s debut album had sold over 1 million records, their second reaching 700,000 units. Savuka received a Grammy nomination for the Best World Music Album in 1993 but disbanded shortly thereafter. Three years later Clegg and Mchunu temporarily re-formed Juluka and recorded Ya Vuka Inkunzi (also released as Crocodile Love). Since then, Clegg has recorded several solo projects including his last album One Life (2007), New World Survivor in 2002 and A South African Story (2003). The Johnny Clegg Band continues to tour worldwide and will return to North America for a 32-city tour in March 2011, which will be a celebration of his 30th year anniversary. Clegg joins Appleseed’s roster of artists active in many social justice causes, including Pete Seeger, Buffy Sainte-Marie, Tommy Sands and Sweet Honey in the Rock.

name: James Blunt
description:
Blunt's first album, "Back to Bedlam," catapulted him into worldwide superstardom on the strength of such massive songs as "You’re Beautiful," "High" and "Goodbye My Lover." His second album, 2007’s "All the Lost Souls," debuted at No. 1 in 10 countries, selling nearly 5 million copies globally and featuring such hits as "1973," "Same Mistake" and "Carry You Home." He has received numerous awards and accolades including two Brit Awards, two World Music Awards, two MTV Video Music Awards, an MTV European Music Award and five Grammy nomination. As he had done on previous concert treks, on his 2008-2009 globe-spanning tour Blunt raised funds for Doctors Without Borders, the international medical humanitarian organization whose work the Sandhurst graduate witnessed first hand as a British military officer stationed in Kosovo. Indeed, as much as he loves making new music, for Blunt, the ultimate joy comes from playing the songs live and sharing them with an audience. And with a new tour starting in 2011, he's looking forward to getting back out there. "Put the album out and get me on tour," he says. "We’re going to have the time of our lives playing these songs." With special guest Christine Perri.

name: Let Me Down Easy
description:
San Diego REPertory Theatre, La Jolla Playhouse, and Vantage Theatre, in Association with Arena Stage, present the Second Stage Theatre’s Production of “Let Me Down Easy,” conceived, written and performed by award-winning playwright and actress, Anna Deavere Smith.

“Let Me Down Easy” explores the power of the body, the price of health and the resilience of the spirit. Based on interviews with an eclectic range of people -- from a heavyweight boxer to a supermodel, and from Texas Governor Ann Richards to legendary cyclist Lance Armstrong.

To write “Let Me Down Easy,” Smith interviewed over 300 people on three continents. “My goal is to learn as much about a person as possible by studying the way they speak,” says Smith. “My portrayals of the more than 20 people in this one-woman show are all drawn from the words of people who speak to the vulnerability of the human body, the resilience of the spirit, the price of care.”

Smith speaks directly to our hopes and discomforts about life, death, whom we should take care of and who should (or should not) take care of us. This show is a bracing, poetic experience you won’t want to miss.

Production will run from April 27, 2011 to May 15, 2011 at Lyceum Stage
79 Horton Plaza
San Diego, CA 92101

Call the Lyceum Box Office at 619-544-1000 or visit www.sdrep.org for show times and to purchase tickets

name: Mexico: Expected/Unexpected
venue: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, La Jolla
description: Mexico: Expected/Unexpected presents over 100 artworks selected from the Isabel and Agustín Coppel Collection, which is one of Mexico’s most comprehensive contemporary art collections. From the poetic to the political, Mexico: Expected/Unexpected showcases the key figures of the Mexican contemporary art scene, including Francis Alÿs, Carlos Amorales, Iñaki Bonillas, Abraham Cruzvillegas, Jorge Méndez Blake, Gabriel Orozco, Damián Ortega, Pedro Reyes, and Melanie Smith. The exhibition contextualizes these artists in relation to noted historical international practitioners, such as Lygia Clark, William Eggleston, Gordon Matta Clark, Ana Mendieta, and Helio Oiticica. Mexico: Expected/Unexpected goes one step further to incorporate the work of cutting-edge international artists working today who share artistic sensibilities and working methods such as Lothar Baumgarten, Maurizio Cattelan, Kendell Geers, Marepe, Rivane Neuenschwander, and Tatiana Trouvé.

Timken Museum of Art Showcases Groundbreaking Robert Wilson Video Portraits
Robert Wilson Video Portraits - February 25 through May 15, 2011

SAN DIEGO – The Timken Museum of Art, which is widely known for its exceptional collection of traditional European and American master paintings, will showcase four of Robert Wilson’s contemporary video portraits from February 25 through May 15, 2011. Admission is free.

Three of the portraits will be displayed on 65-inch high-definition plasma monitors. The fourth will be projected on the west exterior wall of the museum after sunset. The portraits depict recognizable personalities from the world of performing arts including Robert Downey, Jr., Mikhail Baryshnikov, Jeanne Moreau and Winona Ryder who take on an aspect of their professional lives by being captured in character—but in character inspired by great masterpieces of European art.

Robert Downey, Jr., lies as the corpse recalling Rembrandt’s Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Tulp; Mikhail Baryshnikov poses as Saint Sebastian, miraculously preserved from death even though shot through with arrows; Jeanne Moreau stands in velvet alongside a flamboyant inscription as Mary Queen of Scots based on a Nicholas Hilliard painting from 1578; and Winona Ryder is depicted up to her shoulders in a mound of dirt as the character Winnie from Samuel Beckett’s Happy Days.

“These revolutionary portraits in new media use the art of our own time as a means to acquire a greater understanding of the art of the past and of shared concerns that transcend the ages,” said John Wilson, Ph.D., executive director of the Timken. “While a traditional Timken visitor might infer that this exhibition is a departure from the core mission of the museum—a museum devoted to the art of the past—it is precisely because of how these contemporary video portraits are inspired by old master paintings which makes them so trenchant to the Timken’s vision.”

The models appear in near-motionless poses, instructed to “think of nothing,” and to limit any gestures to one or two movements. The result is that it appears to be a still image, but one with almost imperceptible movement by the subjects. The videos are created to be infinite in length, so as to eliminate any narrative beginning or end, approximating a still image. The portraits are accompanied by a discreet, individually composed, soundtrack.

“As with all great portraits, these are poetic biographies of their subjects in addition to likenesses. Inspired by past works of art, history, or popular culture, Wilson’s portraits take a minimalist approach but in a theatrical setting punctuated by dramatic lighting and high production values,” said John Wilson.

A full spectrum of educational programs will be offered to visitors. These include bilingual tours and talks, the Art in the Afternoon lecture series, an Art at Sunset, and an increase in docent hours to allow more tours for schools and the general public. Two Art in the Evening lectures will focus on this exhibition. Art in the Evening lectures bring together national and international art historians, scholars and art connoisseurs with art enthusiasts who want to deepen their understanding of art. These lectures are followed by a reception where participants have the opportunity to interact with guest scholars in an intimate setting amongst the art. In addition, an accompanying publication, part of the Timken’s ongoing series of focus exhibition catalogues, will include a scholarly essay about the exhibition written by former San Diego Union-Tribune art critic Robert Pincus.

Robert Wilson has been described as “a towering figure in the world of experimental theater.” His productions have decisively shaped the look of theater and opera, and with all his work having a profound base in fine arts, his work transcends media and genre. Born and educated in Texas, he moved to New York in 1963 and by the end of the decade was considered a leader of Manhattan’s downtown art scene. His monumental Einstein on the Beach with music by Philip Glass (1976) is widely considered one of the most influential productions of the second half of the 20th century. While Wilson’s earliest work was in theater and opera, he began working in video in the mid-1970s. Influenced by Andy Warhol’s series of three-minute films, Screen Tests, Wilson created a piece called Video 50, with 100 episodes, each 30 seconds long. Among the episodes were portraits of Louis Aragon, the Surrealist poet, and Michel Guy, the French minister of culture at that time. Meeting with Mr. Akio Morita, the head of Sony a few years later in Japan, Wilson shared his idea of life-size vertical video portraits that would break the horizontal screen traditional for televisions. Since that time Wilson’s portraits drew considerable attention and in 2004 Voom HD, a media company specializing in high-definition entertainment, named Wilson its artist-in-residence and commissioned his works. Dissident Industries produces the video portrait works as well as the traveling exhibition.

About the Timken

The Timken Museum of Art, located in San Diego’s Balboa Park, is the permanent home of the highly acclaimed Putnam Foundation’s world-class collection of European and American art and Russian icons. Masterworks in the collection cover 700 years of history and range from 14th century altarpieces through 18th century portraits and landscapes to 19th century still lifes. The works of Italian, Dutch, Flemish, French and American painters are represented, including those of Veronese, il Guercino, Petrus Christus, Jacques-Louis David and John Singleton Copley. The collection also includes the only Rembrandt painting on public display in the area. Considered one of the finest small museums in the world, the Timken Museum of Art is open from 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday and Sundays, 1:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. It is closed on Mondays and major holidays. For more information visit www.timkenmuseum.org; Facebook at Timken Museum of Art or Twitter at @TimkenArtMuseum or call (619) 239-5548.

name: Sweet Storm
description: In 1960 Florida during a ferociously approaching storm, Ruthie and Bo, two newlyweds, enter their honeymoon suite in the sky, a treehouse which is a romantic gesture from the young groom to his bride. Yet Bo’s expectations of living happily ever after in the sky are soon grounded by Ruthie’s realization that marriage comes with many unforeseen – and frightening – challenges. The two lovers struggle to fortify themselves against forces both inside and outside. This is a funny, powerful, and intimate love story to challenge our perceptions of marriage, faith, and love.

name: Botanicals: The Photography of Imogen Cunningham
description: A pioneer of 20th century photography, Imogen Cunningham (1883-1976) played a pivotal role in the acceptance of the medium as an art form and the growth of modernism. She began pursuing photography in 1901 and throughout her long career, maintained an interest in portraiture and nature. Unlike other members of the Western School of Photography who also emphasized nature, such as Edward Weston (1886-1958) and Ansel Adams (1902-84), Cunningham created intimate compositions which call attention to the abstract qualities of nature. This exhibition will feature her black and white botanical photographs from the 1920s-1930s. A preview reception introduces the exhibition on Saturday, January 8, 2011 from 5:00 – 7:00 p.m. Admission at the door is $10 and free for OMA members.

description:

Passover commemorates the story of the Exodus in which the ancient Israelites were freed from slavery in Egypt. On the first night of Passover there is a special meal called a seder filled with ritual to remind us of the significance of the holiday. In this exhibit, local and regional artists creatively interpret through meaning and form the traditional Passover story and ritual objects.

name: COMBS from Asia, Africa and Oceania: A Selection from the Lazar Collection
description:
A diverse collection of hair combs from Asia, Africa and Oceania will be on view in the Parker Gallery from March 5-May 29, 2011. While the obvious use of combs is to clean and straighten the hair, they are also used to keep hair in place and as decorative ornamentation. This exhibition features combs from all over the world in a variety of shapes and materials, including wood, metal, bone and tortoise shell. Added embellishments include beads, shells, feathers, fibers and fabric. Combs are highly visible ornaments used to beautify the wearer, indicate elevated social status and general prestige, as well as expressing cultural knowledge and aesthetic preference.

To schedule a docent tour for your group please call Docent Coordinator Linda Gillen at 760.722.9568. Oceanside Museum of Art is located at 704 Pier View Way in downtown Oceanside within walking distance from the Oceanside Transit Center with Amtrak, Sprinter, Metrolink and NCTD Coaster stops. description: Dr. Tom Dooley was a man who delighted in his sexuality, paid consequences, and yet refused to be defeated, long before ‘Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell’.  Dooley did his residency at Camp Pendleton.  He died young, but was cited by John F. Kennedy for his humanitarian work in Southeastern Asia as an inspiration for the start of the Peace Corps.  Underwritten in part by The James Irvine Foundation and Carlos Malamud.

name: Life of Riley
description: George Riley's closest friends discover that he has just a few months to live and they each deal with the news in their own very surprising way.  George has deeply affected each of their lives and he is now plotting one last final farewell, which could upset all of their futures.

description:

and complex modern-day masterpiece that The New York Times hailed as "flat-out, no asterisks and without qualifications, the most exciting new American play Broadway has seen in years," and that Time Magazine named the Best Play of the Decade.

name: Year Round Whale & Dolphin Watching with Adventure Rib Rides
description:
Within the last week, passengers have enjoyed sightings of Humpback Whales, Fin Whales, Gray Whales and Minke Whales plus lots of dolphin offshore San Diego. Though we are at the tail end of the Gray Whale migration, we will continue to see Humpback and Fin Whales throughout the Spring. We also started seeing Blue Whales as early as May last year. For dolphin lovers, April and May are a great time of year to see baby dolphin.

So, join us today for the adventure of a lifetime on board a fun, fast RIB boat. Excursions are limited to 6 passengers, making for an intimate on-the-water experience. Our knowledgeable captain will serve as your on board naturalist and guide.

Whale and Dolphin Watching Excursions are offered daily in April from 9:00 am - Noon and 1:00 - 4:00 pm.

Adventure Rib Rides is the only charter company in San Diego that offers year round Whale & Dolphin Watching. Humpback and Fin Whales can be seen year round. If you are here during the summer, don't miss the chance to see the largest animal to have ever lived on Earth, the Blue Whale. Blue Whales can be seen offshore San Diego in the Summer and Fall.

Adventure Rib Rides also offers any of our excursions as a private charter.

name: Joan Jonas: The Shape, The Scent, The Feel of Things
venue: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, Downtown
description: Joan Jonas: The Shape, The Scent, The Feel of Things presents a complex five-channel video installation by this seminal video and performance artist. Since the 1970s, Jonas has worked between media, freely incorporating video, movement, music, sculpture, and the spoken word into open-ended narratives. The Shape, the Scent, the Feel of Things returns Jonas to the American Southwest through an artistic consideration of the Hopi snake dance, a ritual which strongly affected her during visits to Arizona in the 1960s. Jonas broadens the associations with references to an essay on the same subject by German art historian Aby Warburg (1866-1929).

name: Strange Bones: Curiosities of the Human Skeleton
description: This exhibition will focus on the many different strange, odd, and curious things that happen to our skeletons.  In addition to information on bone remodeling and adaptation, examples of skeletal congenital anomalies, diseases that disfigure the skeleton, strange healing patterns of traumatic injuries, and cultural modification of the skeleton and teeth will be highlighted.  This exhibition will scientifically focus on how the human skeleton is extremely interesting and adaptable, and will teach our visitors about the biological forces behind certain skeletal diseases and disfiguration.

venue: Coronado Visitor Center and Historical Association & Museum

name: SPACE A Journey To Our Future
description:
SDASM presents Space: A Journey to Our Future, now open for a limited time! Produced by Evergreen Exhibitions and presented in collaboration with NASA, this dynamic, multimedia exhibit looks back into the history of aeronautics and examines the many unknown questions of existence posed by future space exploration.

In December 1972, Apollo 17 took what became one of the most widely publicized and famous images of the twentieth century. The iconic view of Earth as a "Blue Marble" floating in space revolutionized public perception of our fragile planet during the rising environmental consciousness of the early 1970s, highlighting a sense of vulnerability and shared responsibility.

Nearly four decades later, our planet is still a very small and fragile part of a vast universe. We share its destiny, and its limitless possibilities.

Look forward to these out-of-this-world experiences in the exhibit:

  • Explore a future Lunar Base Camp including bunk beds and a kitchen!

  • Build a futuristic space rocket.

  • Create your own mission to Mars.

  • Ride a bike-powered centrifuge and experience the physiological challenges of space flight.

  • Hold a piece of the universe! Touch actual Moon meteorites and Mars rocks.

  • Get an up-close look at artifacts from the space program, and displays on the new spacecraft that can fly you to the Moon and beyond.

  • Meet today's explorers who are working to understand how to protect our planet.

  • Look far into the future of the universe exploration in a 360-degree theatre.

  • Experience the past, present, and future of space through these and dozens of other displays and interactives.

Come explore Space: A Journey to our Future and dare to dream!

name: Jennifer Steinkamp: Madame Curie
venue: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, Downtown
description: MCASD has commissioned Jennifer Steinkamp to create a new work for MCASD Downtown’s Joan and Irwin Jacobs Building.  Entitled Madame Curie, this new commission is inspired by Steinkamp’s recent research into atomic energy, atomic explosions, and the effects of these forces on nature. Marie Curie was the recipient of two Nobel Prizes for creating the theory of radioactivity, and discovering radium and polonium. She was also an avid gardener and lover of flowers. An enveloping panoramic work reminiscent of Steinkamp’s 2004 video projection The Wreck of the Dumaru, the new piece will activate a field of moving flowers and flowering trees in line with the imagery of Steinkamp’s 2010 work Orbit Without Seasons. Flowers rendered realistically for this new work include marsh marigolds, may flower, chestnut blooms, and hop plants, among many others drawn from a list of over 40 plants mentioned in Marie Curie’s biography written by her daughter, Eve Curie. The seven-channel projection will engage the architecture of the space and will require seven synchronized projections onto three walls of the 4,500-square-foot gallery.

name: Annual Del Mar National Horse Show
description:
Elegance, excitement, excellence — these are the hallmarks of the Del Mar National Horse Show, one of the oldest and most prestigious equestrian competitions in the Western United States. The show will run for three weeks starting April 21, 2011 and ending May 8, 2011.

Western competition will be featured the first week, April 21-24; dressage follows April 28-May 1; and hunter/jumper classes conclude the show May 3-8. Each week will have a featured Saturday night evening event.

Whether you enjoy the old-West flavor of Western Week competition, the elegance and grace of Dressage Week, or the thrilling equine athleticism of Hunter/Jumper Week, the Del Mar National Horse Show has plenty to entertain horse lovers of every age.

The Del Mar National began in 1946 as part of the annual San Diego County Fair, which happens each June at the Fairgrounds. By the late 1970s, the Del Mar National had grown so large, it outgrew the confines of the county fair and became a separate event. Western and Hunter/Jumper competition comprised the then two-week show until the early 1990s, when Dressage competition was added as a third week in the show.

Each year, the show attracts more than 1,500 horses of every breed and training, eager to show off what they can do and earn ribbons, trophies, titles and prize money.

What is an Aquathon?

Aqua - meaning water - means a swim. This will be the first discipline of the Aquathon and will be two to twenty lengths of the pool, depending on which distance you decide on. Aquathon - sounds like triathlon - yep, that's right, it is similar to a triathlon, but instead of having three different disciplines (swim, bike and run) we have two. A swim in the pool and then a run departing from the pool and ending at the running track.

description:
The simply chic tour will allow you to peek inside four-of-a-kind San Diego hotels while sampling some of the most delectable treats. As you walk along the brick streets marveling at the numerous historical buildings, So Diego Tours will share architectural delights and stories about the spicier side of life in the Gaslamp Quarter in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Included on the tour are the following boutique hotels:

The Keating Hotel: Nothing even remotely resembling a chain hotel will be found inside The Keating Hotel. The first architectural endeavor of Pininfarina, the designer of the Ferrari and the Maserati, is one of the most unique hotels in existence...a work of art that honors the past and relishes the modern. Your imagination will run wild when you walk through the incredibly cool rooms in this former high-class brothel.

Ramada Inn: Formerly the St. James Hotel, the Ramada Inn & Suites is a charming historic boutique hotel overflowing with charm. Built in 1913, the St. James was the city’s first luxury high-rise hotel. We’ll step back in time as we take a ride in the antique twin elevators, at one time the fastest in town. Once we reach the tenth floor, we’ll enjoy the twin delights of a delicious tasting and a gorgeous view.

Hotel Indigo: No detail was overlooked in the creation of this state-of-the-art Gaslamp treasure. This green boutique hotel takes pride in honoring the environment and providing visitors with a healthy and rejuvenating atmosphere. And, you won’t find a much better place to sip on a cocktail than the terrace bar with gorgeous views of PETCO Park and the Gaslamp Quarter.

Andaz Hotel: Although operated by the Hyatt hotel chain, there is nothing corporate about the Andaz Hotel. Released from their cages, the staff at this fresh boutique hotel walks the floor looking for ways to satisfy your every need. Home to more stunning art and another premiere roof deck, the Andaz is a visual and sensual treat.

In 1975 King Clave debuted Raul Velasco's Siempre en Domingo (Always on Sunday) and continues to perform shows across the world. Composer and singer Leo Dan (Leopoldo Dante Tevez) has recorded more than 20 albums during his long career between Argentinia and Mexico.

His appreciation for Mexican music led him to record with mariachis and the reception this music received from the Mexican public helped boost his international fame. Some of the greatest hits from Leo Dan include Como te Extrano, Mi Amor, Mari es Mi Amor, Celia, Pideme la Luna and Toquen Mariachis, Cante, to name a few. He currently lives in the United States.

name: "The Sky Tonight" Planetarium Shows
description:
"The Sky Tonight" is the Reuben H. Fleet Science Center's monthly live planetarium show in the newly renovated Heikoff Dome Theater. "The Sky Tonight" takes place at 7:00 p.m. and 8:00 p.m. on the first Wednesday of each month. The May presentation will explore "Virgo Cluster."

During each month's show, audiences also explore a different interesting topic in astronomy, such as supernovas, constellations or black holes.

Weather and operational requirements permitting, the San Diego Astronomy Association provides free telescope viewing outdoors following the Fleet's planetarium show. This is a separate free event--planetarium show tickets are not required.

Due to the darkness required in the theater and the sophisticated nature of the material presented, “The Sky Tonight” show is not recommended for children 5 years and under. Tickets to the planetarium shows are sold on a first-come, first-served basis. Fleet Members may make advance reservations by calling (619) 238-1233 ext. 810. It is recommended that all others arrive at the Science Center by 6:30 p.m. to purchase tickets for this popular program. Tickets for “The Sky Tonight” include a visit to the Exhibit Galleries.

name: Exploring Ethics Lecture: "Who Owns Your Cell Phone?" at the Reuben H. Fleet Science Center
description:
Exploring Ethics Lecture - in conjunction with the Center for Ethics in Science and Technology, the Fleet invites guests to encounter science from an ethical perspective.

Lecture: “Who Owns Your Cell Phone?” – The first part of this talk examines the fact that a cell phone, by itself, is useless; without the cooperation of the operator, the sales and service network, subsidies and the like, it would be an expensive and useless brick. As cell phones become more like computers, they rely more and more on diverse infrastructure, and many of the players have conflicting goals. Much frustration can be traced to this tension. The second part of the talk examine the fact that, as phones become much more like computers, they become targets for hacking and various kinds of attacks on their security. (Hackers refer to "owning" their targets.) Greg Rose, Senior Vice President, Office of the Chief Scientist at QUALCOMM Inc. examines some of the security issues and possible consequences of a breach.

To attend, RSVP to 858-822-2647. 5:30 – 7:00 pm, Reuben H. Fleet Science Center Community Forum.

name: Intimate Whale Watching Tours Without the Crowds
description:
Whale Watching with Sail San Diego is incredible experience, where the groups are small, and our experienced Captains/Trained Naturalists are the best in the business!

This is a great trip and experience for all ages! We are very conscious of our environment and carefully follow the rules of whale watching and have a huge respect for these magnificent mammals and the journey they are on! We run environmentally responsible trips, something we feel is so important.

Because we run small groups on one of our two beautiful 40’ Catalina's, you and your guests and family can have an intimate time on the water and have all your questions about the grey whale and the whale migration answered by our knowledgeable Trained Naturalists who have a wealth of information and love to share all they know with our guests. We also keep whale watching literature on the boats that is easy and fun to read. Not sitting on a microphone far away from guests, our Captains are right there to help you experience nature at its best. The Captains who are in arms reach look for Whales, Dolphins, Porpoise, Sea Lions and Pelagic Sea Birds. Captains will tell you about the plant-life and actually do a hands-on demo for kids and show them all the signs to look out for while looking for whales or dolphins. Not only is this trip informative it is FUN!!

Last year there were very few trips where no whales were spotted but we always guarantee sea lions! We will work with you on a second trip if no whales are spotted- most of the time this is not the case! Whale Watching trips are scheduled twice a day. We do a morning whale watching trip and a mid-day whale watching trip. Times vary because we know some of our guests are here on business and have schedules and itinerary’s to keep. Call us for times and details.

All the trips offer complimentary beverages which include beer/wine, non-alcoholic beverages and nice hot-chocolate for those chilly days! Snacks are also provided for guest to enjoy while under way. To ensure the comfort of each guest we also provide extra jackets, blankets, foul-weather gear, hats, gloves, sunscreens, for those who forget – sunglasses. All of this is there for our guests to enjoy and we encourage everyone to be as comfortable as possible. Enjoy the whale watching literature on the boats, sit back, relax and enjoy the most memorable time on the water possible.

name: Rounding Third
description:
Scripps Ranch Theatre will present Richard Dresser’s “Rounding Third,” a hilarious and tumultuous journey of two very different Little League coaches through an entire season, from their first tentative meeting to the climactic championship game.

"Rounding Third" opens May 21 and runs through June 25 at Scripps Ranch’s theater on the Alliant International University campus.

Although the dialog is between Little League coaches, the play asks important societal questions: how should we raise our children and what does it mean to be an American man in today’s society.

Directed by Robert May, “Rounding Third” features John Nutten as Don and Walter Murray as Michael, the two coaches with often conflicting views. Jenn Tyrer is the production and stage manager.

May directed last season's acclaimed "I'm Not Rappaport for SRT," as well as this season’s production of "Painting Churches." As a director, his credits include the Patté Award-winning "A Prayer For My Daughter" and the Billie Award-winning Pinter duo "Ashes to Ashes" and "The Lover at 6th@Penn."

Robert earned a master of fine arts degree from the University of Arizona and a bachelor of arts degree from Southern Illinois University-Carbondale.

John Nutten received his bachelors degree at UCLA’s school of Film, Television and Theatre. He has performed locally in many shows including, "Prayer For My Daughter" at 6th & Penn Theatre, "1776" at Lamb’s Player’s Theatre, "Breaking Legs" at North Coast Rep, and "Twelfth Night" with New Village Arts.

Walter Murray has performed on stages in San Diego, Los Angeles and New York. He is a co-founder of the San Diego Black Ensemble Theater, and a former member of the Board of the Actors Alliance of San Diego.

"Rounding Third opened off Broadway in 2003 at the John Houseman Theater and received enthusiastic reviews: “Two coaches - one a veteran, the other a new recruit - and their markedly different personal circumstances and philosophies about the game…drive this funny, acerbic and touching play through the bumpy terrain of fatherhood and baseball." (Playbill) “You will recognize your neighbor, your brother, and maybe yourself." – (nytheatre.com)

Performances are on Fridays and Saturdays at 8:00 pm and Sundays at 2:00 pm Scripps Ranch Theatre encourages patrons to make reservations early as performances sell out quickly.

For reservations, call the Scripps Ranch Theatre box-office at 858-578-7728 or visit our website at www.scrippsranchtheatre.org for additional information.

Location: All performances are held in the Legler Benbough Theatre on the campus of Alliant International University (formerly United States International University) on Avenue of Nations in Scripps Ranch, one-half mile east of the I-15/Miramar-Pomerado Road exit.

Scripps Ranch Theatre, now in its 32nd year, consistently produces high-quality and entertaining theater and has earned a reputation as one of the finest small theaters in San Diego.

name: Autumn Gem Film Screening
venue: San Diego Chinese Historical Society and Museum
description:
The San Diego Chinese Historical Museum is pleased to present a screening of the documentary film, Autumn Gem 秋瑾.

Discover how one woman overcame the sexist oppression of traditional China to become an accomplished writer, skilled martial artist, and leader of a revolutionary army in the struggle to free her nation from imperial rule.

In the late 19th century, many Chinese struggled to end the corrupt and oppressive Qing Dynasty, but few outside China realize that one woman stood out among their number. Qiu Jin (秋瑾 1875-1907) was not only an activist for women’s rights; she also fought and died as a martyr, struggling to found a modern Chinese nation. As China’s first feminist, Qiu Jin is a familiar heroine in China, but Autumn Gem is the first American-produced documentary to share Qiu Jin’s story with English-speaking audiences.

Using interviews with scholars, archival materials, and dramatic recreations based on Qiu’s original writings, two San Francisco Bay Area Chinese American filmmakers, Rae Chang and Adam Tow, produced and directed this film. It stars former China National Wushu Champion and Hollywood stunt actress Li Jing, and some footage actually was shot at the San Diego Chinese Historical Museum. The directors also partnered with the San Francisco Chinese Culture Center and the Official Qiu Jin Museum in Shaoxing 紹興, China.

The screening will be held in the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Extension building at 328 J Street on Saturday, May 28th from 1:00 to 3:00 pm. Refreshments will be served at the reception held in the Chinese garden at 404 Third Avenue.

The San Diego Chinese Historical Museum is located at 404 Third Avenue in downtown San Diego. For more information, please visit our website at www.sdchm.org.

name: Joan Jonas: The Shape, The Scent, The Feel of Things
venue: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, Downtown
description: Joan Jonas: The Shape, The Scent, The Feel of Things presents a complex five-channel video installation by this seminal video and performance artist. Since the 1970s, Jonas has worked between media, freely incorporating video, movement, music, sculpture, and the spoken word into open-ended narratives. The Shape, the Scent, the Feel of Things returns Jonas to the American Southwest through an artistic consideration of the Hopi snake dance, a ritual which strongly affected her during visits to Arizona in the 1960s. Jonas broadens the associations with references to an essay on the same subject by German art historian Aby Warburg (1866-1929).

name: SPACE A Journey To Our Future
description:
SDASM presents Space: A Journey to Our Future, now open for a limited time! Produced by Evergreen Exhibitions and presented in collaboration with NASA, this dynamic, multimedia exhibit looks back into the history of aeronautics and examines the many unknown questions of existence posed by future space exploration.

In December 1972, Apollo 17 took what became one of the most widely publicized and famous images of the twentieth century. The iconic view of Earth as a "Blue Marble" floating in space revolutionized public perception of our fragile planet during the rising environmental consciousness of the early 1970s, highlighting a sense of vulnerability and shared responsibility.

Nearly four decades later, our planet is still a very small and fragile part of a vast universe. We share its destiny, and its limitless possibilities.

Look forward to these out-of-this-world experiences in the exhibit:

  • Explore a future Lunar Base Camp including bunk beds and a kitchen!

  • Build a futuristic space rocket.

  • Create your own mission to Mars.

  • Ride a bike-powered centrifuge and experience the physiological challenges of space flight.

  • Hold a piece of the universe! Touch actual Moon meteorites and Mars rocks.

  • Get an up-close look at artifacts from the space program, and displays on the new spacecraft that can fly you to the Moon and beyond.

  • Meet today's explorers who are working to understand how to protect our planet.

  • Look far into the future of the universe exploration in a 360-degree theatre.

  • Experience the past, present, and future of space through these and dozens of other displays and interactives.

Come explore Space: A Journey to our Future and dare to dream!

name: Jennifer Steinkamp: Madame Curie
venue: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, Downtown
description: MCASD has commissioned Jennifer Steinkamp to create a new work for MCASD Downtown’s Joan and Irwin Jacobs Building.  Entitled Madame Curie, this new commission is inspired by Steinkamp’s recent research into atomic energy, atomic explosions, and the effects of these forces on nature. Marie Curie was the recipient of two Nobel Prizes for creating the theory of radioactivity, and discovering radium and polonium. She was also an avid gardener and lover of flowers. An enveloping panoramic work reminiscent of Steinkamp’s 2004 video projection The Wreck of the Dumaru, the new piece will activate a field of moving flowers and flowering trees in line with the imagery of Steinkamp’s 2010 work Orbit Without Seasons. Flowers rendered realistically for this new work include marsh marigolds, may flower, chestnut blooms, and hop plants, among many others drawn from a list of over 40 plants mentioned in Marie Curie’s biography written by her daughter, Eve Curie. The seven-channel projection will engage the architecture of the space and will require seven synchronized projections onto three walls of the 4,500-square-foot gallery.

All-Inclusive Price Only $68 per person!
Meeting Place: Empress Hotel in the Village of La Jolla.

3 hr. Beer & Food Guided Walking Tour includes*:
• Award-Winning Beer Tastings
• VIP Food Pairings e.g. burgers, pizza, mac n cheese!
• 3-4 Tasty tour stops
• Beer Games and Prizes!

For Reservations Contact:
858-551-5115
shira@lajollawinetours.com

name: Making a Difference in the Lagoon - Del Mar Fairgrounds
description:
Join us to make a difference in the San Dieguito Lagoon, next to the Del Mar Fairgrounds, by rehabilitating the habitat for the hundreds of birds and other species that call it home.

Our activities are suitable for all ages and we welcome individuals, school groups, community service organizations and corporate employees who want to volunteer with us.

Tools, training and work gloves provided! Please bring water, sun protection and wear sturdy, closed-toed shoes. Reservations are required for all volunteer events. Please contact volunteer@sdrvc.org or 858-674-2275 ext. 12 to reserve a space and for directions.

Date: April 17, 2011
Time: 1:00 – 3:30 pm
Location: North Bank Restoration site, San Dieguito Lagoon
Activity: We will be removing invasive, non-native plants to protect wildlife habitat

Date: May 22, 2011
Time: 10:00 am – 12:00 pm
Location: North Bank Restoration site, San Dieguito Lagoon
Activity: We will be removing invasive, non-native plants to protect wildlife habitat

Date: June 26, 2011
Time: 1:00 – 3:30 pm
Location: Crest Canyon, Del Mar
Activity: We will be removing invasive, non-native plants to protect wildlife habitat, and maintaining new restoration areas

Date: July 31, 2011
Time: 1:00 – 3:30 pm
Location: Crest Canyon, Del Mar
Activity: We will be removing invasive, non-native plants to protect wildlife habitat, and maintaining new restoration areas

name: 14th Annual Chrysler Classic Speed Festival
description: This spectacular family-oriented auto racing event is situated on the runways and taxiways of the Naval Air Station North Island and combines the unique draw of vintage race cars on a Navy installation that also showcases the latest Naval aircraft and equipment. With the stunning San Diego Bay as the backdrop, 225 of the world's most unique vintage vehicles will race, some worth millions of dollars, and fans will be able to get up close and personal with the cars and their drivers. 8am to 4pm.

name: Journey to the Lost Temple Mini-Musical
description: Journey to the Lost Temple is an interactive and hilarious musical adventure at LEGOLAND® California.  The 25-minute mini-musical includes up to 25 volunteers and transports audiences back in time to ancient Egypt and Cleopatra’s lost temple. To return home, audience members must help the show’s action hero, Johnny Thunder, find a lost time machine. The show takes place in Playtown Theater Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays Jan. 22-June 3; daily April 16-23 and June 4-Sept. 5; weekends only Sept. 10-Oct. 30. The show is included in the price of LEGOLAND admission.

name: “Datsuzoku”
venue: Japanese Friendship Garden of San Diego
description: The Japanese Friendship Garden presents “Datsuzoku” a selection of photographs by Rachel Blaser. The exhibit will be featured in the Garden from June to July. These images are intended to be a reflection of Japanese aesthetics, with a focus on the interplay of familiarity and strangeness in the perception of an outsider.

name: Wings Over Gillespie Air Show
description: San Diego's biggest civilian air show includes re-enactments of WWII and Vietnam War aerial battles with pyrotechnic displays, 40 aircraft (flying and static displays), live entertainment, a Kidz Zone and food and merchandise vendors.

name: World Ocean’s Day at SEA LIFE™
description:
SEA LIFE™ Carlsbad Aquarium next to LEGOLAND® California hosts a party with a purpose as it celebrates World Oceans Day on Saturday, June 4. The goal of the World Oceans Day Party at SEA LIFE is to raise awareness of conserving and protecting our oceans in a fun and playful way. The World Oceans Day Party takes place from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm and promises interactive fun for the entire family.

All activities are included in the price of Aquarium admission.

name: Summer C-Note
description:
San Diego Art Institute: Museum of the Living Artist is proud to present

Summer C-Note Event
It is time once more for the most anticipated, lively and capricious of fundraisers…
C-Note consists of original artwork - donated by our members, emerging regional artists, and sold right off the wall for one ($100), two ($200) or three ($300) C-Notes.

It gives new and experienced art collectors alike an opportunity to purchase original works at less-expensive prices.

Don’t miss the C-Note Night on June 4, 2011, 5:00 - 8:00 pm
Preview Only: June 3 and 4, 2011 10:00 am - 4:00 pm
C-Note runs: June 3 - June 19, 2011
The SDAI’s C-Note Fundraiser benefits many programs
For more information call: 619-236-0011

The San Diego Art Institute is located in Balboa Park, House of Charm, and 1439 El Prado. Hours: Tuesday - Saturday 10:00 am - 4:00 pm. Sunday 12:00 - 4:00 pm. Requested Gallery Donation: Adults $3. Senior Citizens, Military and Students $2. Children under 12 admitted free.

name: San Diego County Fair
description:
This isn't your typical county fair! The view from the San Diego County Fair Ferris Wheel alone - overlooking the blue Pacific - sets us apart from most fairs. We have all of the outlandish fried foods on-a-stick you know and love, plus exquisite gardens, livestock barns, endless exhibits, and a top-notch midway complete with carnival rides. In addition, the San Diego County Fair boasts 8 stages, programmed with some of the most quality entertainment Southern California has to offer!

Visit our website at www.sdfair.com/entertainment for a complete entertainment listing.

name: Santa Maria Creek Exploration
description:
Experience a rare, privately owned, slice of natural San Diego and learn about the biology, geology and cultural history of the area from local experts. This rugged hike moves from the Pasqual Valley, up Santa Maria Creek toward the Ramona Grasslands and includes hidden pools, massive boulders, towering cliffs overhead, and a wide variety of plants and wildlife.

Date: Sunday, June 11, 2011
Time: 9:00 am - 2:00 pm
Location: Santa Maria Creek, Escondido
Distance: 3.5 miles
Price: Members $25
Hike is a benefit for New Conservancy members at the $35 level or above

To ensure a quality experience for participants, group size is limited. Reservations are required.

To Register for an Exploration: Contact sdrvc@sdrvc.org or 858-755-6956, or register securely online at sdrvc.org/news_events/ (Please be sure to select San Dieguito Exploration from the first drop down menu located 3rd from the bottom).

More information is available at sdrvc.org/news_events/, or 858-755-6956, or sdrvc@sdrvc.org.

This exploration is part of the non-profit Conservancy’s San Dieguito Explorations fundraising series.

name: San Diego Potters' Guild Spring Sale
description:
Looking for unique gifts? Visit the San Diego Potters’ Guild’s (SDPG) sale in Balboa Park. Located in the Park’s Spanish Village patio area, the sale features thousands of pieces of hand-made ceramics by many of San Diego’s finest potters.

All of the items at the sale are one-of-a-kind. Works range from functional ware such as plates, bowls, and coffee cups to more decorative and sculptural forms such as ceramic shoes, garden lanterns, and conch shells. Prices range from a few dollars to a few hundred dollars.

In addition to buying hand-made ceramics, you can also meet the artists. Most of the Guild members will be available to answer questions about ceramics in general or their own work in particular. There will also be demonstrations of throwing pots on the wheel.

name: Mengini Winery's 9th Annual Barrel Tasting
description: More than a dozen San Diego vintners pour tank and barrel samples of unreleased wines for pairing with festive foods, as guests enjoy live music on the scenic grounds of Menghini Winery in Julian. 12:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.

name: National City Day at San Diego County fair
description:
Sunday, 10:00 am - 5:00 pm

Local exhibits showcasing the best of National City including booths from local businesses, National City Chamber of Commerce, City Government, Musicians, Police and Fire Department.

name: SEA LIFE™ Father’s Day Celebration
description:
SEA LIFE™ Aquarium Carlsbad is celebrating fathers on Saturday, June 18 with a special Father’s Day crafting activity taking place from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm. The special crafting event is included in the price of SEA LIFE admission.

The mission of SEA LIFE Aquarium at LEGOLAND® California Resort is to immerse guests in an interactive, educational and fun aquarium experience while increasing awareness of the importance of safeguarding the sea and its inhabitants. Packed with interactive play zones, fun activities and unforgettable sights, guests are sure to experience amazing discoveries at SEA LIFE Aquarium.

name: LEGO® STAR WARS™ Days
description:
LEGO® STAR WARS™ Days return to LEGOLAND® California and promise to be bigger and better than ever this year! Join other STAR WARS fans for product viewing, building activities and giveaways and mingle with your favorite STAR WARS characters from the 501ST Legion of Stormtroopers. May the Force be with you at LEGOLAND!

All STAR WARS Days activities are included in the price of LEGOLAND admission.

name: 9th Annual Beer and Sake Festival
description:
The 9th Annual Beer and Sake Festival, presented by the Japan Society of San Diego and Tijuana (JSSDT), will bring together San Diego’s top chefs to showcase their Japanese culinary and sake traditions for the San Diego community. The festival will highlight imported Japanese beers and local microbrews and many flavors, styles and varieties of sake. In addition to the tastings, the festival will feature culinary creations from the most talented chefs in San Diego. Top San Diego restaurants will display signature dishes and sushi creations. Guests can enter to win prizes during a raffle and silent auction as the San Diego Taiko drum group performs throughout the evening. Proceeds from the event will support the JSSDT’s educational programs.

Admission to the festival is $60 per person or $40 for JSSDT members and can be purchased online at www.japan-society.org

name: San Diego Spirits Festival
description:
Come see what everyone is buzzing about!

San Diego Spirits Festival is a two-day celebration of spirits, cocktails and local culture - the only event of its kind on the West Coast. The 3rd Annual Festival will take place at an exhilarating new venue – the stunning Port Pavilion Pier on Broadway– an expansive oasis surrounded by the sparkling San Diego Bay.

With Cocktail Competitions, 2 Days of Grand Tastings, Educational Seminars, VIP after-parties, and other fabulous and unexpected surprises, the San Diego Spirits Festival is designed to be an event that offers a one-of-a-kind and unforgettable experience!

Get in the spirit and enjoy a rare chance to learn about some of the world’s most innovative brands from the most knowledgeable experts both locally and from around the world.

Mark your calendar and come for one or both days with unlimited tastings of fine spirits, cocktails, food and other surprises.

Where would you rather be?
